title: A global complete intersection has the expected dimension at every point
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $m,t\ge0$ integers, $Q=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f_1,\dots,f_t\in Q$ and $T=Q/(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. Assume $T\neq0$ and that the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is $\dim T=m-t$. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset T$ the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at the point $\mathfrak p$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}T)=m-t$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00S8 (section-lci, line 35806), the paragraph following Definition 00S9 (definition-lci-field, line 35817), lines 35834-35849: 'we conclude that dim(S_m) = n - c for all maximal ideals of S and that Spec(S) is equidimensional of dimension n - c, see Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field)', with Lemma 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Lemma 00KW (lemma-one-equation); used in the proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph ('t = m - dim(S_g)')

proof.text: (Setup.) Write $J=(f_1,\dots,f_t)\subseteq Q$, $\pi:Q\to T=Q/J$ for the quotient map and $X=\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. $T$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\pi$ being a surjection of $k$-algebras from the polynomial ring $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. A field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, both finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $Q=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]/(0)$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Since $T\neq0$ it has a maximal, hence prime, ideal, so $X\neq\emptyset$ and $m-t=\dim X\ge0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (a one-point set $\{\mathfrak p\}$ has closure $V(\mathfrak p)$, an irreducible closed subset, giving a chain of length $0$).

source.place: Algebra, paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35834-35849, and the proof of Lemma Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field, lines 27787-27852)

proof.text: (Upper bound.) Let $\mathfrak p\in X$. The whole space $X$ is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, so by the definition of the Krull dimension at a point as the minimum of $\dim U$ over open neighbourhoods $U\ni\mathfrak p$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim_{\mathfrak p}X\le\dim X=m-t$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (the hypothesis).

proof.text:
(Every open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ contains a closed point; the Jacobson argument of 00OT.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be open with $\mathfrak p\in U$. The closed subsets of $X$ are the sets $V(I)=\{\mathfrak q:I\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$, $I\subseteq T$ an ideal [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], so $U=X\setminus V(I)$ for some ideal $I$. As $\mathfrak p\in U$, $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$: pick $g\in I$ with $g
otin\mathfrak p$. Since $T$ is a finite type $k$-algebra (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal] gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak M\subset T$ with $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak M$ and $g
otin\mathfrak M$. Then $I
ot\subseteq\mathfrak M$, i.e. $\mathfrak M
otin V(I)$, so $\mathfrak M\in U$.

proof.text: ($\dim T_{\mathfrak M}\ge m-t$ at every maximal ideal; 00OP and 00KW.) Let $\mathfrak M\subset T$ be a maximal ideal and $\mathfrak M'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak M)\subset Q$. Then $Q/\mathfrak M'\cong T/\mathfrak M$ is a field, so $\mathfrak M'$ is a maximal ideal of $Q$, $J\subseteq\mathfrak M'$, and $\mathfrak M=\mathfrak M'/J$ under $T=Q/J$. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension], $\dim(Q_{\mathfrak M'})=m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim(Q_{\mathfrak M'})$ is the supremum $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M')$ of the lengths of chains of primes of $Q$ whose last member is contained in $\mathfrak M'$, and $\dim(T_{\mathfrak M})$ is the supremum $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M)$ of the lengths of chains of primes of $T=Q/J$ whose last member is contained in $\mathfrak M=\mathfrak M'/J$. (c) $Q$ is Noetherian (step 1) and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in J\subseteq\mathfrak M'$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] (with $R=Q$, $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak M'$) gives $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M')\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M'/J)+t$. Together: $m\le\dim(T_{\mathfrak M})+t$ in $\{0,1,\dots,\infty\}$, hence $\dim(T_{\mathfrak M})\ge m-t$ (if $\dim(T_{\mathfrak M})=\infty$ this is trivial; otherwise subtract $t$). (This is the source's application of 00OP and of 00KW $t$ times, made at the level of heights.)

proof.text: (Lower bound and conclusion.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak M\in U$ the maximal ideal of step 3. Then $U$ is also an open neighbourhood of the point $\mathfrak M$, so by the definition of the dimension at a point as a minimum [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim U\ge\dim_{\mathfrak M}X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] (applied to the finitely generated $k$-algebra $T$, step 1, and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$), $\dim_{\mathfrak M}X=\dim(T_{\mathfrak M})$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], which is $\ge m-t$ by step 4. Hence $\dim U\ge m-t$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] for every open neighbourhood $U$ of $\mathfrak p$, so their minimum satisfies $\dim_{\mathfrak p}X\ge m-t$. With step 2, $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}T)=m-t$.

Statement kept. Proof in five steps following the source: setup (T finite type, Q Noetherian, m - t >= 0); upper bound dim_p X <= dim X; every open neighbourhood of p contains a maximal ideal M (Jacobson, 00G1 node), as in the proof of 00OT; dim T_M >= m - t at every maximal M by 00OP (new unsplit node) and 00KW applied t times, written as Krull's height bound ht(M') <= ht(M'/J) + t (new Mathlib leaf Ideal.height_le_height_add_encard_of_subset), converted to dimensions of localizations by the existing leaf for dim R_p = height; lower bound via the existing node 00OU (dim at a closed point = dim of the local ring). Equidimensionality and irreducible components are not needed: only 00OT's direction (1) >= (3) is used, written out. The hypothesis dim T = m - t is used only for the upper bound. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension (00OP, unsplit, Mathlib has only the global dim k[x_1..x_n] = n; candidate recorded), lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound (Mathlib leaf).
